accepted.s: The Citizenship (Amendment) Act, 2019 was passed by Parliament in which month and year?
accepted.x: The Citizenship (Amendment) Act, 2019 was passed by Parliament in December 2019.
accepted.tq: Use the precise date-based recall approach.
accepted.sec: CAA 2019 - passage, countries, communities, cut-off date, exempted areas

accepted.s: The Citizenship (Amendment) Act, 2019 came into force on:
accepted.x: The Act came into force on 12 December 2019. The rules were notified later, on 11 March 2024.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the commencement date of an Act from the date of notification of its rules.
accepted.sec: CAA 2019 - passage, countries, communities, cut-off date, exempted areas

accepted.s: The Citizenship (Amendment) Rules, 2024 were notified on:
accepted.x: The rules under the Citizenship (Amendment) Act, 2019 were notified on 11 March 2024.
accepted.tq: Separate the parent legislation from its rules through date discrimination.
accepted.sec: CAA 2019 - passage, countries, communities, cut-off date, exempted areas

accepted.s: Under the Citizenship (Amendment) Act, 2019, eligible migrants must have entered India on or before:
accepted.x: The cut-off date for entry into India is 31 December 2014.
accepted.tq: Test the exact cut-off date rather than the date of enactment.
accepted.sec: CAA 2019 - passage, countries, communities, cut-off date, exempted areas

accepted.s: Which one of the following groups correctly represents the countries covered by the Citizenship (Amendment) Act, 2019?
accepted.x: The Act covers migrants from Afghanistan, Bangladesh and Pakistan.
accepted.tq: Use country-list discrimination among neighbouring countries.
accepted.sec: CAA 2019 - passage, countries, communities, cut-off date, exempted areas

accepted.s: Which of the following communities is NOT included among the communities specified under the Citizenship (Amendment) Act, 2019?
accepted.x: The specified communities are Hindu, Sikh, Buddhist, Jain, Parsi and Christian. Muslims are not included in the specified list.
accepted.tq: Find the excluded community in a closely related list.
accepted.sec: CAA 2019 - passage, countries, communities, cut-off date, exempted areas

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Citizenship (Amendment) Act, 2019:
1. Citizenship under the provision is deemed to take effect from the date of entry into India.
2. The residence requirement for naturalisation was reduced to five years.
3. The Third Schedule to the Citizenship Act was amended.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. The Act gives citizenship effect from the date of entry, reduces the naturalisation residence requirement to five years and amends the Third Schedule.
accepted.tq: Combine date, duration and statutory-schedule facts in a coded statement question.
accepted.sec: CAA 2019 - passage, countries, communities, cut-off date, exempted areas

accepted.s:
Which of the following areas are exempted from the operation of the Citizenship (Amendment) Act, 2019?
1. Tribal areas covered by the Sixth Schedule in Assam, Meghalaya, Mizoram and Tripura
2. Inner Line Permit areas in Arunachal Pradesh, Nagaland, Mizoram and Manipur
3. All districts of West Bengal
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: The Sixth Schedule tribal areas in the four specified States and Inner Line Permit areas in the four specified States are exempt. All districts of West Bengal are not exempted under this provision.
accepted.tq: Identify the two recognised exemption categories and reject an overbroad claim.
accepted.sec: CAA 2019 - passage, countries, communities, cut-off date, exempted areas

accepted.s: Under the Citizenship (Amendment) Rules, 2026, an approved CAA applicant holding a Pakistani, Afghan or Bangladeshi passport is required to surrender that passport within:
accepted.x: The foreign passport must be surrendered within 15 days of approval under the 2026 Rules.
accepted.tq: Use a duration-based numerical trap with nearby time periods.
accepted.sec: CAA 2019 - passage, countries, communities, cut-off date, exempted areas

accepted.s: The constitutional validity of the Citizenship (Amendment) Act, 2019 has primarily been challenged with reference to:
accepted.x: The challenge principally invokes Article 14, particularly concerning classification based on religion and country.
accepted.tq: Match the constitutional challenge with the relevant Article.
accepted.sec: CAA 2019 - passage, countries, communities, cut-off date, exempted areas

accepted.s: Who has the exclusive power to make laws regulating citizenship in India?
accepted.x: Article 11 empowers Parliament to make laws regarding acquisition and termination of citizenship and all other matters relating to citizenship.
accepted.tq: Apply the 'who would do this job?' method to constitutional powers.
accepted.sec: Competent authority to regulate citizenship - article and body

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly distinguishes the roles of the Union Home Ministry and the Election Commission in citizenship matters?
o: The Election Commission alone regulates acquisition and termination of citizenship.
The Home Ministry frames citizenship rules, while the Election Commission checks citizenship for electoral rolls.
The Home Ministry checks electoral rolls, while the Election Commission frames citizenship rules.
Both bodies jointly prescribe all conditions of citizenship.
accepted.x: The Union Home Ministry frames citizenship rules, whereas the Election Commission checks citizenship in relation to electoral rolls under Article 324.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between two authorities by matching each body with its specific function.
accepted.sec: Competent authority to regulate citizenship - article and body

accepted.s: The Citizenship Rules, 2009 were framed by the:
accepted.x: The Union Ministry of Home Affairs frames the Citizenship Rules, including the Citizenship Rules, 2009.
accepted.tq: Use the ministry-function association trap.
accepted.sec: Competent authority to regulate citizenship - article and body

accepted.s: Which of the following countries follow the principle of dual citizenship at the national and sub-national levels?
o: The United States of America and Switzerland
accepted.x: The United States and Switzerland recognise national as well as state or cantonal citizenship. India follows single citizenship.
accepted.tq: Use a confusable country-comparison pair.
accepted.sec: Single vs dual citizenship - Indian position, other countries, domicile

accepted.s: India's system of single citizenship was borrowed chiefly from the constitutional practice of:
accepted.x: The Indian Constitution adopted the idea of single citizenship from Britain. Canada also follows single citizenship.
accepted.tq: Test the source of a borrowed constitutional feature.
accepted.sec: Single vs dual citizenship - Indian position, other countries, domicile

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. India provides for one citizenship for the Union and the States.
2. The Constitution recognises a separate constitutional domicile for every State.
3. Article 9 is associated with the prohibition of voluntary acquisition of foreign citizenship.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: India has single citizenship and Article 9 deals with voluntary acquisition of foreign citizenship. The Constitution does not recognise a separate State domicile in the constitutional sense.
accepted.tq: Use one reversed domicile statement to test the single-citizenship concept.
accepted.sec: Single vs dual citizenship - Indian position, other countries, domicile

accepted.s: Which of the following documents is NOT conclusive proof of Indian citizenship?
o: Certificate of citizenship issued under law
accepted.x: Aadhaar is not proof of citizenship. A passport is a travel document and is also not, by itself, conclusive proof of citizenship; voter ID and ration cards are likewise not citizenship proof.
accepted.tq: Distinguish identity or travel documents from conclusive citizenship documents.
accepted.sec: Single vs dual citizenship - Indian position, other countries, domicile

accepted.s: A person who is a foreign citizen of Indian origin, or the spouse or child of such a person, may generally be eligible for:
accepted.x: Foreign citizens of Indian origin, their spouses and children may be eligible for an Overseas Citizen of India card, subject to statutory conditions.
accepted.tq: Identify the legal status from the eligibility description.
accepted.sec: OCI cardholder - eligibility, who is barred, rights not available

accepted.s: Which one of the following persons is barred from eligibility for an OCI card?
o: A foreign citizen whose ancestor was an Indian national
A child of an eligible person of Indian origin
A spouse of an eligible person of Indian origin
accepted.x: Foreign military personnel are barred from OCI eligibility. Persons connected with Indian origin may otherwise qualify subject to the prescribed conditions.
accepted.tq: Find the statutory exclusion among otherwise eligible categories.
accepted.sec: OCI cardholder - eligibility, who is barred, rights not available

accepted.s:
OCI cardholders are barred from which of the following rights?
1. Voting in elections
2. Contesting elections
3. Holding constitutional offices
4. Public employment as a general rule
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: OCI cardholders are not Indian citizens and do not have voting rights, the right to contest elections, eligibility for constitutional offices or public employment as a general rule.
accepted.tq: Use a comprehensive rights-and-disqualifications list.
accepted.sec: OCI cardholder - eligibility, who is barred, rights not available

accepted.s: Which one of the following statements regarding an OCI cardholder is correct?
o: An OCI cardholder is an Indian citizen with restricted voting rights.
An OCI cardholder is entitled to contest elections but cannot hold public employment.
An OCI cardholder may obtain lifelong visa-free entry, but the OCI card does not confer citizenship.
An OCI cardholder can hold any constitutional office except that of President.
accepted.x: An OCI card provides lifelong visa-free entry, but an OCI holder remains a foreign citizen and is not an Indian citizen.
accepted.tq: Separate OCI status from Indian citizenship and associated political rights.
accepted.sec: OCI cardholder - eligibility, who is barred, rights not available

accepted.s: The OCI card alone has been sufficient for lifelong visa-free entry into India since:
accepted.x: Since 2016, the OCI card alone has been sufficient for lifelong visa-free entry into India.
accepted.tq: Test a specific implementation year against nearby policy dates.
accepted.sec: OCI cardholder - eligibility, who is barred, rights not available

accepted.s:
Which of the following was introduced under the Citizenship (Amendment) Rules, 2026 in relation to OCI services?
1. E-OCI cards
2. A central OCI database
3. Online application and renunciation facilities
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: The 2026 Rules introduced e-OCI cards, a central OCI database and online application and renunciation facilities.
accepted.tq: Treat a set of administrative reforms as a single coded list.
accepted.sec: OCI cardholder - eligibility, who is barred, rights not available

accepted.s:
Arrange the following in chronological order of their formation or attainment of the stated status:
A. Andhra State
B. Andhra Pradesh
C. Mizoram as a State
D. Telangana
Select the correct answer.
accepted.x: Andhra State was formed in 1953, Andhra Pradesh in 1956, Mizoram became a State in 1987 and Telangana was formed in 2014.
accepted.tq: Fix the earliest and latest events first, then place the middle events by year.
accepted.sec: Formation of states and UTs → year and Act/amendment, chronology

accepted.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Andhra Pradesh — Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act, 2014
accepted.x: Andhra State was formed on 1 October 1953 under the Andhra State Act, 1953. Andhra Pradesh was formed in 1956 and Telangana in 2014 under different instruments.
accepted.tq: Match the unit with the correct formation Act, avoiding swapped instruments.
accepted.sec: Formation of states and UTs → year and Act/amendment, chronology

accepted.s: Sikkim became an associate State in 1974 and a full-fledged State in 1975 through, respectively:
accepted.x: The 35th Amendment introduced Sikkim as an associate State, while the 36th Amendment made it a full State in 1975.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between two consecutive constitutional amendments.
accepted.sec: Formation of states and UTs → year and Act/amendment, chronology

accepted.s: Mizoram became a State on 20 February 1987 under the:
o: State of Mizoram Act, 1986, together with the 53rd Amendment
accepted.x: Mizoram attained Statehood on 20 February 1987 under the State of Mizoram Act, 1986 and the 53rd Constitutional Amendment.
accepted.tq: Match the Statehood date with both the statute and amendment.
accepted.sec: Formation of states and UTs → year and Act/amendment, chronology

accepted.s: Telangana was formed on 2 June 2014 under the:
accepted.x: Telangana was formed on 2 June 2014 under the Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act, 2014.
accepted.tq: Use the State-formation Act association as the decisive clue.
accepted.sec: Formation of states and UTs → year and Act/amendment, chronology

accepted.s: The Union Territories of Jammu and Kashmir and Ladakh came into existence on:
accepted.x: The Union Territories of Jammu and Kashmir and Ladakh came into existence on 31 October 2019 under the Jammu and Kashmir Reorganisation Act, 2019.
accepted.tq: Reject the one-year-shift trap in a date-based question.
accepted.sec: Formation of states and UTs → year and Act/amendment, chronology

accepted.s:
India may acquire foreign territory through which of the following means?
1. Cession
2. Treaty
3. Conquest
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: As a sovereign State, India may acquire foreign territory through cession, treaty or conquest. Puducherry and Goa are examples associated with acquired territories.
accepted.tq: Use a complete list of constitutionally relevant territorial modes.
accepted.sec: Territory of India vs Union of India

accepted.s: Article 2 of the Constitution deals with Parliament's power to:
o: Abolish the office of the Governor
Admit or establish new States not forming part of India
Alter the name of an existing State only
accepted.x: Article 2 concerns the admission or establishment of new States into the Union, such as the constitutional treatment of Sikkim.
accepted.tq: Distinguish Article 2 from Article 3 by the status of the territory involved.
accepted.sec: Articles 1-4 number game

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding a Bill under Article 3:
1. It can be introduced only on the recommendation of the President.
2. The President refers it to the affected State legislature for its views.
3. The views of the State legislature are binding on Parliament.
4. It is passed by a simple majority.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Statements 1, 2 and 4 are correct. The views of the affected State legislature are sought but are not binding on Parliament.
accepted.tq: Identify the non-binding consultation statement among procedural conditions.
accepted.sec: Articles 1-4 number game

accepted.s: Laws made under Articles 2 and 3 of the Constitution are:
o: Ordinances issued exclusively by the President
Ordinary laws and are not deemed amendments under Article 368
Subject to approval by every affected State legislature
Amendments under Article 368 requiring a special majority
accepted.x: Article 4 provides that laws made under Articles 2 and 3 are not treated as constitutional amendments under Article 368.
accepted.tq: Test the exception to the general constitutional-amendment procedure.
accepted.sec: Articles 1-4 number game

accepted.s: The States Reorganisation Commission constituted in 1953 consisted of:
o: B.R. Ambedkar, K.M. Munshi and H.N. Kunzru
K.M. Panikkar, Jawaharlal Nehru and B.R. Ambedkar
Fazl Ali, Sardar Patel and Rajendra Prasad
Fazl Ali, K.M. Panikkar and H.N. Kunzru
accepted.x: The 1953 States Reorganisation Commission was chaired by Fazl Ali, with K.M. Panikkar and H.N. Kunzru as members.
accepted.tq: Recall a committee through its complete membership combination.
accepted.sec: States Reorganisation Commission and Act 1956

accepted.s:
Arrange the following events in chronological order:
A. Constitution of the States Reorganisation Commission
B. Formation of Andhra State
C. Enactment of the States Reorganisation Act
D. Formation of Andhra Pradesh
Select the correct answer.
accepted.x: The Commission was constituted in 1953, Andhra State was formed in 1953, the Act was enacted in 1956 and Andhra Pradesh was formed on 1 November 1956 under that reorganisation.
accepted.tq: Place same-year events before the 1956 Act and State formation.
accepted.sec: States Reorganisation Commission and Act 1956
